title: Career Roadmap · Maritime Logistics Manager
summary: A Maritime Logistics Manager coordinates the movement of goods through ports, shipping lines, freight forwarders, customs processes, warehouses and inland transportation networks. The role ensures cargo moves safely, cost-effectively and on schedule while meeting documentation, regulatory and customer requirements.

about.text: Ports, shipping offices, logistics hubs, warehouses and corporate operations centres

about.label: Typical Entry Route

about.text: Maritime Logistics Manager → Head of Shipping Operations / Supply Chain Director

blocks.text: A Maritime Logistics Manager coordinates the movement of goods through ports, shipping lines, freight forwarders, customs processes, warehouses and inland transportation networks. The role ensures cargo moves safely, cost-effectively and on schedule while meeting documentation, regulatory and customer requirements.

Unlike a shipboard officer, a Maritime Logistics Manager usually works in shore-based commercial and operational environments. The role focuses on cargo movement, shipping schedules, transport coordination, cost control, documentation, vendor management and supply chain performance.
Key Responsibilities

items.text: Coordinate import, export and international shipping operations.
Manage shipping schedules, cargo bookings and transport arrangements.
Coordinate with shipping lines, freight forwarders, ports, customs brokers and transport providers.
Monitor cargo movement from origin to destination.
Ensure shipping documentation is accurate and complete.
Track container availability, demurrage, detention and port-related charges.
Plan logistics costs, negotiate vendor rates and manage service-level agreements.
Resolve delays, cargo discrepancies, documentation issues and shipment exceptions.
Monitor key performance indicators such as on-time delivery, freight cost and turnaround time.
Use transport management systems, enterprise resource planning systems and logistics dashboards.
Support compliance with applicable customs, trade, safety and environmental requirements.

blocks.text: The strongest route to becoming a Maritime Logistics Manager is to combine a relevant degree with hands-on shipping operations experience, practical documentation knowledge, freight-cost control and strong analytical skills.

Students should initially target Shipping Operations Executive, Logistics Coordinator or Freight Forwarding Executive roles. From there, they can build expertise in carrier management, port operations, procurement, analytics and team leadership before progressing toward Maritime Logistics Manager.

The key differentiator is the ability to manage shipments end to end—not just understand logistics theory—and to demonstrate measurable improvements in cost, delivery reliability, documentation quality and customer service.
